text: Case Number from the OSHA Log
Injury Description - Describe Activities of Employee When Injury or Illness Occurred and What Tools, Machinery, Objects, Chemicals, Etc. Were Involved.
answer: Employee was transferring boxed inventory from a pallet to shelving in aisle 12 using a manual pallet jack and a step stool. While lifting a 35-lb box, he stepped onto a wet spot on the concrete floor and slipped, contacting the metal edge of the rack with his right forearm and twisting his lower back. Items involved: manual pallet jack, corrugated boxes, metal storage racking, step stool, safety gloves.

text: What Happened to Cause This Injury or Illness? (Describe How The Injury Occurred)
answer: A condensation leak near the cooler created a wet area on the floor. While turning with a box in hand, the worker slipped, lost balance, and fell against the shelving, resulting in a cut to the right forearm and a strained lower back.

text: What Was The Injury or Illness? (State the Part of Body Affected and How It Was Affected)
answer: Acute lumbar strain with muscle spasm and reduced range of motion; 3-cm laceration to the right forearm requiring six sutures. No fractures per X-ray.
